context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix for work order creation verified. The fix removed stock checks so: (1) Main WO always creates when user requests manufacturing, (2) Child WOs always create for items that have active routings. FG-001 has routing 35ef9031-bb5c-4dd5-87c1-5c6834104a4d, SA-001 has routing 5fdf4d44-2001-412c-a4d5-16d330af44bf. SA-002 does NOT have a routing so no child WO is created for it. The Work Orders table shows parent-child hierarchy with └ symbol for child WOs.

rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: Previously create_wo_for_item() checked stock levels and skipped WO creation if stock was sufficient. This prevented main WO and child WOs from being created even when user explicitly requested manufacturing.
rca_of_the_issue.fix_applied: Removed stock check logic. Main WO always creates (user explicitly requested manufacturing). Child WOs always create for items that have active routings (needed for this production run).
rca_of_the_issue.verification: Created 13 pytest tests that verify: (1) Main WO always created, (2) Child WOs created for items with routings, (3) Start WO consumes materials, (4) Complete WO updates stock, (5) Parent-child relationships maintained
